item.title: Belgian unions lead protest against austerity policies as government's future hangs in balance
item.description: Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his resignation to the king on 2 November over the budget impasse, but the monarch refused to accept it and gave him more time to find a solution.

item.title: Encore! Madrid's Teatro Real named world's best opera theatre for second time
item.description: The Teatro Real in Madrid has won the prize for the world’s best opera house at the International Opera Awards in Vienna. It's the second success for the Spanish institution. Its artistic director Joan Matabosch praised the staff and described the theatre as being in the top division.

item.title: EU targets Chinese imports in fresh trade defence investigation
item.description: The EU investigation could lead to sweeping tariffs or quotas on materials used in defence, renewable energy and transport, as Brussels steps up efforts to protect European industry from cheap Chinese imports.

item.title: Antimicrobial resistance is a health security threat. Europe can lead global action
item.description: Antimicrobial resistance is killing thousands in Europe, and experts say only coordinated EU “fair share” funding and pull incentives can revive drug innovation.

item.title: Ukraine: Dramatic night rescue pulls woman from rubble after 22 hours
item.description: An elderly woman was rescued alive after spending 22 hours trapped beneath concrete slabs in Dymer, north of Kyiv. The death toll from Sunday's Russian strike on an apartment building has risen to 11.

item.title: Airfares in Europe to stay ‘largely stable’ in 2027, new forecast suggests
item.description: The Air Monitor 2027 report predicts that economy seats for inter-European flights will increase between 0.3% and 0.4%.

item.title: India pledges €1.4bn to help Nepal rebuild after deadly glacier flood
item.description: Balendra Shah's first visit to a neighbouring country since becoming prime minister also brought agreements on a railway, a hydropower plant and fuel infrastructure.

item.title: Spain's 29 November election: Shielding the vote from hybrid threats and disinformation
item.description: Disinformation, cyberattacks and the geopolitical use of migration put Spain in the sights of foreign powers. Experts urge shielding key sectors and speeding a joint European response to election interference.

item.title: Armenia to link power network with Azerbaijan and Turkey for AI energy
item.description: Armenia's prime minister announces electrical interconnections with Turkey and Azerbaijan, while Nvidia’s Rev Lebaredian warns of AI’s rising energy needs.

item.title: GTA 6 breaks sales records as Trump administration co-opt game and get ridiculed online
item.description: The release of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI has already broken all records... and led the Trump administration to hijack the cultural moment via AI-generated posts.

item.title: Indonesia: Rescuers recover 24 body bags from burnt-out factory
item.description: A devastating fire has gutted a confectionery factory near Jakarta, with authorities recovering 24 body bags from the wreckage. Rescue workers continue searching for missing employees as investigators examine the cause.

item.title: Germany restaurant owner plans women's shifts around menstrual cycles
item.description: Many women work through their periods despite severe pain. One restaurateur from the Allgäu exempts affected female staff from duty. But how much consideration is appropriate at work?

item.title: Armenia's AI Silk Road aims to reconnect East and West
item.description: With a new computing power centre, international collaborations and a robotics lab, the small South Caucasus country seeks to turn its technological talent into greater economic influence.

item.title: Málaga, Lisbon, Madrid: These are the best cities in Europe for expats
item.description: In Europe, five cities made the top 10 for expats – including three in Spain.

item.title: Over 10,000 migrants reach Spain's Canary Islands in a record November as El Hierro hits capacity
item.description: Spain's Maritime Rescue Service and Civil Guard have escorted five boats to the port of La Restinga and located a sixth. The island is now housing around 900 migrants after a record-breaking November.

item.title: Does the European Union need more data centres? Take our poll
item.description: Does the EU need to invest more in data centres? To become a key player in artificial intelligence, it needs a lot more computing infrastructure to get there.

item.title: Brazil: Colourful costumes and dancing take over Copacabana Pride
item.description: Thousands of people filled Copacabana's beachfront in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on Sunday 22 November 2026, for the city's 31st Pride Parade, celebrating LGBT+ diversity and calling for greater equality.

item.title: Thousands evacuated after 'unknown substance' released at UK Don Toliver concert
item.description: Emergency services were called after "reports of people in the crowd suffering effects from an unknown substance", said Manchester police, which declared a major incident at the scene.

item.title: Turkish authorities search for lion spotted on outskirts of Istanbul
item.description: The National Parks Directorate said specialist veterinarians and teams equipped with thermal imaging cameras were assisting the search, which was focused on a wooded area.

item.title: How will AI change travel and tourism? What it could mean for how we plan and book holidays
item.description: As AI becomes increasingly embedded within travel, research weighs in on its potential, the challenges and whether travellers are willing to completely put their trust in the developing technology.

item.title: Sanctions, summits and strikes: The war in Ukraine shows no sign of slowing
item.description: Good morning. Leo Cendrowicz here, bringing you the Monday newsletter. This week, we’re dealing with more bombing of Ukraine, and the metaphorical bombing of the COP31 climate talks in Turkey.

item.title: Champs-Élysées launch Christmas lights season and revive Paris Christmas market
item.description: On Sunday 22 November, the Avenue des Champs-Élysées officially entered the end-of-year festive season by switching on its traditional Christmas lights.

item.title: Can Europe's data centres go green? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot
item.description: Europe plans to triple its data centre capacity over the next five to seven years, but by 2030, it could use more than 3% of its energy, straining power grids and water resources. How can the EU grow its AI capacity while staying sustainable? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot.

item.title: Portugal joins Europe's top 10 for tech investment on back of Tekever funding round
item.description: Tekever's funding round has decisively contributed to accelerating investment in Portugal, which is expected to grow 187% this year. The country is gaining ground in the European landscape, following the broader trend of recovery in technological investment in the rest of Europe.

item.title: Europe Today: COP31 talks collapsed over omission of fossil fuels
item.description: After days of negotiations, COP31 meeting in Antalya, Turkey ended without reaching consensus. We explore the consequences for the planet with Ciarán Cuffe, co-chair of the European Green Party. We also speak with General Seán Clancy, Chairman of the EU Military Committee.

item.title: Satellite images show Russian warship capsized in Libya after suspected Ukrainian drone strike
item.description: Satellite images show a Russian naval vessel capsized at the port of Benghazi in eastern Libya following an explosion on Sunday. Local authorities suspect a drone attack but have not confirmed who was responsible.

item.title: North Korea's leader highlights 'sovereignty' after rebuffing Trump offer for talks
item.description: Trump left Asia on Thursday after a landmark summit with the Chinese and Russian presidents, without meeting Kim, as Trump had suggested he might.

item.title: Nearly €15 billion in new investments announced at 'Choose France' summit
item.description: More than 273 industrial projects representing €14.9 billion in investment are highlighted on Monday at the 'Choose France' summit for French companies. Yet behind the figures lies a dynamic marked by uncertainty.

item.title: Russian air strikes kill at least 15 people across Kyiv region, Ukraine says
item.description: Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year.

item.title: Wind sails, e-methanol and a stalled global deal: Can hard-to-decarbonise shipping go green?
item.description: A year after Trump stalled a global net-zero shipping deal, the IMO is trying again – with wind power, batteries, e-fuels and LNG in the mix.

item.title: Income inequality across Europe: Where is it highest and how is it changing?
item.description: Income inequality in the EU fell slightly in 2025, but the gap between rich and poor still varies widely across Europe. Euronews Business takes a closer look at how it is changing and why.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 23rd, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 23rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: December 2026 travel guide: Europe’s best places to visit, what to see and things to do
item.description: From chasing the Northern Lights in Swedish Lapland to exploring Europe’s best Christmas markets or taking a festive train journey, here’s what to see and where to go this December.

item.title: Ukraine responsible for drone strikes on two Russian ships off Libya, Zelenskyy says
item.description: The attacks came after a drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday, close to the waters of Finland, whose border guard said the strike was Ukrainian.

item.title: US intelligence chief warns of more tech outages as Delta suffers fresh Atlanta failure
item.description: The warning comes as Americans face a growing run of failures affecting air travel, Microsoft email services, major banks and the National Security Agency's network.

item.title: Taiwan warns Canada against deeper China trade ties as Carney seeks to diversify
item.description: The warning came days after Carney met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, where the two sides agreed further tariff cuts as Canada looks for new markets as Trump's trade war continues.

item.title: Tech back in the firing line as traders track Wall Street rout
item.description: Ahead of European markets opening, Asian stock markets struggled to recover from last week's sell-off, with tech firms again in the firing line as investors tracked an eye-watering rout on Wall Street.

item.title: Who is Gevorg Tamamyan, the youngest candidate to lead the WHO?
item.description: Armenian paediatric oncologist Gevorg Tamamyan told Euronews he is campaigning to lead the WHO with a focus on equity, restoring trust and bringing an outsider's perspective to the organisation.

item.title: Nine people injured after gunfire at central California concert
item.description: The sheriff's department said it believes the shooting "may be gang-related" but gave no further detail.

item.title: Morocco: A surreal sculpture park turns the world upside down
item.description: An upside-down house, giant furniture and vegetable-headed figures await visitors at Ramakech, an 11-hectare sculpture park near Marrakech, where French artist Jean-François Fourtou brings childhood memories to life through extraordinary, larger-than-life installations.

item.title: Midterms: US Democrats secure biggest House majority in decades
item.description: Democrats have secured their largest US House of Representatives majority in more than three decades, dealing a crushing blow to President Donald Trump and setting the stage for two years of divided government, political confrontation and ambitious legislative battles.

item.title: Finland confirms Russia is towing drone-hit cargo ship after Baltic Sea attack
item.description: Russian authorities begin towing a damaged military-linked cargo vessel after a suspected Ukrainian drone attack near Finnish waters, highlighting growing security risks in the Baltic Sea.

item.title: Germany tests Kamikaze drones and AI targeting technology in Lithuania
item.description: The Bundeswehr's latest military trials highlight Germany's growing investment in unmanned weapons, artificial intelligence and preparations to defend NATO's eastern flank.

item.title: Marc Márquez wins eighth MotoGP title in Portugal, surpassing Rossi's record
item.description: The Spanish rider is crowned top-category champion in Portugal after a historic comeback in an injury-hit season. He now has ten world titles, eight in the top class.

item.title: French interior ministry rocked by probe into prefect's leaks to National Rally
item.description: Suspected of informing the RN about probes into the party, the top official asked to be relieved of his post. He condemns a "manhunt", while Marine Le Pen says she has "never received confidential information" from him.

item.title: Polls put Spain's PP ahead of PSOE a week before 29 November election
item.description: Polls by Ipsos, Data10, GAD3 and Hamalgama Métrica all place the PP as the leading force, though they differ on the gap to the socialists and far-right Vox’s result. All four surveys suggest a right-wing coalition would secure a majority.

item.title: Turkey prosecutors seek asset freezes on 108 high-profit traders
item.description: Turkish prosecutors have sought asset freezes on 108 high-profit traders amid a $17 billion investment fund scandal involving alleged market manipulation and political connections.

item.title: Tanker incident “involving military forces” reported in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Amid conflicting reports that an Iranian tanker departed Iran’s Kharg Island on Sunday to force the US military blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, an incident was reported near the US navy blockade line. Iran threatened that any US attempt to stop its tankers would result in immediate attacks.

item.title: Israel forecast to grow 4.5%: What can Europe learn from its tech boom?
item.description: Israel's tech-powered economy is set to overtake Sweden and Ireland to become the world's 25th-largest in 2026, the IMF says, amid years of war. As European and Israeli policymakers gather in Jerusalem this week to discuss closer ties, what can Europe learn from its innovation model?

item.title: Suspected drone strike hits Russian ship at Libya’s Benghazi port, raising regional security concerns
item.description: A suspected drone strike on a Russian ship at Libya’s Benghazi port has raised concerns over the spread of the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Authorities are investigating the blast amid growing fears for regional security.
